facts.fact: OTR (One-Time Registration) must be completed on the SSC website ssc.gov.in before applying for an exam
facts.quote: All the candidates who wish to apply in response to this Notice are required to complete their One-Time Registration (OTR) on the website of the Commission (https://ssc.gov.in).

facts.fact: An OTR made on the old website ssc.nic.in does not work on the new website, so it must be done again on ssc.gov.in
facts.quote: The OTR generated on the old website (https://ssc.nic.in ) will not be functional for the new website.

facts.fact: After OTR the candidate fills the online application form for the exam; one OTR stays valid for all exams applied for on the new website
facts.quote: Subsequent to OTR, the candidates can proceed to fill in the Online Application Form for the Examination. Once an OTR has been generated on the new website (https://ssc.gov.in), it will continue to remain valid for all the Examinations to be applied for on the new website.

facts.fact: The application form is submitted only online, on ssc.gov.in or through the mySSC mobile app
facts.quote: The Application Form must be submitted only in online mode, either at the website of SSC (HQ) (https://ssc.gov.in) or through the ‘mySSC’ mobile application

behaviour: Explains OTR and then the exam application on ssc.gov.in (or the mySSC app), with citation to the SSC notice.
fail_if: Says the old ssc.nic.in registration still works, or describes an offline application.
summary: SSC notice (02.09.2026): OTR on ssc.gov.in is mandatory (old ssc.nic.in OTR invalid), valid for all exams; then apply online on ssc.gov.in or mySSC app.
